<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>



</system-reminder>

# Worker Base Procedures

You are a worker in a multi-agent mission. This skill defines the procedures that ALL workers must follow. After completing startup, you'll invoke your specific worker skill for the actual work procedure.

## Your Assigned Feature

Your feature has been pre-assigned by the system and is shown in your bootstrap message. The feature includes:
- `id` - Feature identifier
- `description` - What to build
- `skillName` - The skill you must invoke for the work procedure
- `expectedBehavior` - What success looks like
- `fulfills` - Validation contract assertion IDs (if present)

**Your feature's `fulfills` field lists validation contract assertions that must be true after your work.** Read these assertions carefully before starting — they define what "done" means for your feature. Before completing, ensure that each assertion would pass. If you realize an assertion cannot be fulfilled given your current scope, flag it in your handoff.

- **Prefer narrower test selection over output truncation.** If output is too noisy, run a more targeted test pattern (e.g., `npm test -- --testPathPattern MyFile`) instead of piping through `head`/`tail`.

#### Skill Feedback (help improve future workers)

Before calling EndFeatureRun, reflect on whether you followed your skill's procedure:

- **Service won't start or healthcheck fails** - manifest may be broken or external dependency missing

Do not spin endlessly trying to fix infrastructure issues you can't resolve.
- Blocked by missing dependency, unsatisfied preconditions, or unclear requirements
- Previous worker left broken state you can't fix

#### When You Cannot Validate Your Work

If you cannot actually verify your work because of an environment or access blocker — e.g. the app is logged out and you can't authenticate, a page won't load, a service is unreachable, credentials are expired, or the agent-browser session never becomes ready — you must NOT report `successState: "success"`, and you must NOT silently defer the unverifiable check into a vague follow-up feature for "later".

# Integration and boundaries

**What belongs here:** the worktree lifecycle, the integration procedure step by step, the shared files only
the integration feature writes, the reports and session-log entries produced at each boundary, how usage is
measured and priced, the budget caps and throttle behaviour, and what the human answers. Sources:
`planning-notes.md` "Execution model" and notes 8-9, `architecture.md` §16, `SPEC.md` §2, §9, §10,
`reports/README.md`, `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` entries 24-26, `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`.

**What does not belong here:** CI job definitions and how to read runs (`github-and-ci.md`), test procedures
(`user-testing.md`).

## Paths and names

- Repository (mission branch `mission/observatory-v1`): `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory`
- Worktrees: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/<m>` on branch `wt/<m>`, `<m>` in
  `s, m0, m1, m2, m3, m4, m5`.
- Stable symlink used by `services.yaml`: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current`.
- Workers and validators of `<m>` edit only inside `wt/<m>`. Two worktrees never edit the same file (rule 13).

## Worktree lifecycle (commands)

Create the worktree for milestone `<m>` (orchestrator at mission start for S; the integration feature for
every later milestone):

```sh
REPO=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
WT_ROOT=/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt
mkdir -p "$WT_ROOT"
git -C "$REPO" worktree add "$WT_ROOT/<m>" -b "wt/<m>" mission/observatory-v1
ln -sfn "$WT_ROOT/<m>" "$WT_ROOT/current"
git -C "$WT_ROOT/<m>" branch --show-current        # wt/<m>
sh /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c/init.sh   # verifies hooks, branch, symlink
```

Workers commit on `wt/<m>` and push it (`git -C "$WT_ROOT/<m>" push -u origin "wt/<m>"`); `mission-branch.yml`
does not run on `wt/**`, so `make check` in the worktree is the worker's gate. Remove the worktree only after
integration (its branch stays as history):

```sh
git -C "$REPO" worktree remove "$WT_ROOT/<prev>"
git -C "$REPO" worktree prune
```

## Integration procedure (integration feature, first feature of each milestone after S)

Skill `integration-worker`; runs on the mission branch in the repository checkout, never in a worktree.

1. Preconditions: the previous milestone's validators passed with zero blocking findings; `make check` is
   green in `wt/<prev>`; `wt/<prev>` is pushed.
2. Merge, no fast-forward:

   ```sh
   cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
   git status --short            # clean, on mission/observatory-v1
   git merge --no-ff wt/<prev> -m "Integrate <prev>: <one line of what landed>"
   ```

   A conflict means rule 13 was violated: resolve it in a new commit on the mission branch and record it in
   the boundary report (`docs/runbooks/stalled-mission.md`, `integration.conflict`).
3. `make check` on the mission branch (exit 0 required). From M0 also `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80`, alone.
4. Decision files due at this boundary (`docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
   context, decision, alternatives, consequences), then `make decisions-index`. Due at S integration:
   session schema and mapping input (fixture header carries `droid --version`; sidecar for usage and children),
   keyring variant B, backlog is `BACKLOG.md` only, coverage, machete, read-only token (Actions runs and
   commit statuses instead of Checks).
5. Shared files, written only here: `SPEC.md` §9 (one `F-NNN` row per owner feedback, with date, applies-to,
   status) and §10 (one row per integrated milestone: integrated date, what landed, tests green, usage spent,
   deviations, unknown events left), `SPEC.md` amended as-built where a note or decision changed it (rule 8),
   `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md` (new `B-NNN` rows with reason and earliest; settled rows marked done with the
   date, dropped rows struck through), `docs/decisions/README.md` (generated), `reports/usage/<m>.md`,
   `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json`, `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md`, `reports/README.md` index lines.
6. Session log entry in `ai/session/<date>-session.md` (style below), and `build-log/<day>/*.jsonl` committed
   as they are.
7. Commit (subject at most 72 characters, co-author trailer), push `mission/observatory-v1`, wait for
   `mission-checks` green (`gh run watch`, then `gh run view <id> --json createdAt,updatedAt,conclusion` for
   the wall time); paste the run id and times into `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` (one more commit if the report
   is written after the run; the second push produces a second run, which is noted).
8. Record the owner's unlocked-display screenshot path in the boundary report (the owner takes it at this
   boundary, planning note 4).
9. Remove the old worktree, create `wt/<next>`, repoint `current` (commands above), run `init.sh`.
10. Return the boundary report to the orchestrator: what landed, tests green, `make check` and
    `mission-checks` results with ids, usage spent against the cap, deviations proposed with reason and cost,
    unknown events left, decisions written, open questions for the owner. The human answers only here or
    when the stall flag is up (rule 15).

Final M5 integration and the single PR `mission/observatory-v1` to `main` are the one feature of milestone
`final` (`integration-worker`, `final-integrate-m5-and-open-pr`): it also writes `reports/waste/m5.md` with
`observatory-cli metrics` on the mission's own capture and verifies the Process section of the contract
(VAL-PROC-001..037). It opens the PR, waits for `gate`, confirms `mergeStateStatus CLEAN` and hands over; the
owner merges and the branch is deleted at the merge.

## Reports at each boundary (`reports/README.md` conventions)

Numbers pasted from the tools that produced them (rule 7); the README indexes each file with a one-line
description.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `reports/usage/<m>.md` | tokens per role and model (input, output, cache read, cache write, thinking), Factory credits when visible, cost at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, waste by cause, wall time of the milestone, the cap and the remainder; source named (usage page or `.settings.json` fields) |
| `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` | Agent Readiness report re-run at integration (`/readiness-report`, B-015); existing: `2026-10-22-baseline.json` (Level 1, 5 of 65), `2026-10-22-scaffold.json` (Level 3, 31 of 65), `2026-10-22-actions.json` (36 of 66) |
| `reports/ci/<date>-<m>.md` | the `mission-branch` run on the integration push: run id and URL, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, wall time, per-job durations, warm or cold, against the 3-minute budget (SPEC §7, rule 11) |
| `reports/readiness/<date>-<label>.md` | prose findings (readiness-style) when a milestone produced measured facts worth keeping, e.g. attach latency or Leptos go/no-go evidence |

The owner's screenshot path for the milestone is referenced from `reports/usage/<m>.md` (or the boundary
report) with its byte size.

## Session log entry style (`ai/session/<date>-session.md`)

The file is excluded from markdownlint (`ignores: ai/session/**`) because it records text verbatim. Entries
24-26 set the pattern:

- Heading `## Entry N — <short title>` (em dash), numbered consecutively across the day.
- Bold lead-ins as paragraphs, in this order when they apply: `**Owner message (verbatim):**` or
  `**Owner answers (verbatim):**` as a bullet list quoting the owner word for word; `**Edits applied ...:**`
  listing each file and what changed in it; `**Shipping:**` (branch, target, who merges);
  `**Shipped:**` or `**Outcome:**` with bullets naming full commit SHAs and subjects, PR numbers with URLs,
  run ids with URLs and conclusions, pasted times (`wall time 9 min 19 s, pasted from gh run view`),
  per-job durations, `make check` exit code and what was skipped and why.
- Corrections to earlier entries are stated in the later entry ("Correction to entry 24: ..."), never edited
  in place.
- Owner decisions are listed with the artefact they produce ("decision file at S integration").
- Transcript pointers: the session ids of the workers involved
  (`Worker session 82ad1581-fe75-4436-ac9c-9bc1e20a789b (dependency readiness)`).
- The entry that introduces itself names its own commit ("Commit: the commit that introduces this entry").

## Usage measurement and pricing

Unit: USD-equivalent at `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`, computed from token counts Factory reports for the

2. The sidecars of the mission's sessions under

   cacheCreationTokens, thinkingTokens, factoryCredits`; `model` and `reasoningEffort` give the price row.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Throttles and caps (planning note 8)

At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour, 7-day or monthly limit) or at a milestone cap: the run pauses at the
point reached, usage so far is written to `reports/usage/<m>.md` (marked partial), the stall flag goes up and
the owner is asked. Spending beyond a cap is a deviation (rule 9) and waits for approval. **No silent model or
reasoning-effort downgrade, ever**: any model or effort change is a decision file (rule 19). Workers that hit
a throttle mid-feature leave the worktree in a committed state (red test committed, work-in-progress described
in the handoff) and report; nothing is amended or stashed.

# services.yaml: single source of truth for the commands and local services of the
# droid-observatory mission (mission id e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c).
#
# Every command runs from the active milestone worktree through the stable symlink
#   WT = /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current  -> observatory-wt/<m>, branch wt/<m>
# The repository checkout (mission branch mission/observatory-v1) is
#   REPO = /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory
# and is touched only by init.sh (make doctor, make hooks) and by the integration feature.
#
# Concurrency rules (measured 2026-10-22, reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md,
# SPEC.md §5.8, AGENTS.md "Runtime limits"):
#   - At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve`
#     (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each, CPU negligible idle). Use `--session <name>` per validator.
#   - `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 -> 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run);
#     it builds under $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/llvm-cov-target, so it does not wait on the build lock
#     and competes for CPU instead.
#   - All cargo builds (cargo test, trunk, cargo tauri dev) serialize on the shared
#     CARGO_TARGET_DIR lock (/home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target, from the shell environment):
#     "Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory" is a wait, not a failure.
#   - Exactly one `trunk serve` owns port 3141. `cargo tauri dev` starts its own trunk on 3141
#     through beforeDevCommand; stop trunk-ui before starting tauri-dev. The trunk started by
#     tauri-dev also serves agent-browser on 3141 (verified: curl on 3141 answered while the
#     Tauri window was up).
#   - Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
#   - Validators run user tests only after builds finish.
#
# Ports: 3141 = UI dev server (one trunk at a time); 3142-3149 = scratch (a second trunk, a
# test HTTP server, etc.). Off-limits: 5000, 7000, 8000, 11434, 18444-18451 and anything already
# listening (owner's Ollama, SurrealDB, Docker and other services). See library/environment.md.
#
# Machine: 10 cores, 64 GB RAM, baseline 1-min load 3-10 (readiness run: `load averages: 3,05 6,26 9,34`).
# The readiness report's 70 % headroom rule allows at most 7 cores for builds; CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is set
# to 6 below so one build leaves room for the LLM-driven agent loops, trunk and the browser sessions.

env:
  # Parallel rustc jobs per cargo invocation. 6 of 10 cores: under the 7-core headroom budget
  # and leaves CPU for the agent processes and servers that run alongside a build.
  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: "6"
  # Line-coverage floor for observatory-core (SPEC §6, B-005). S reports it; the M0 integration
  # enforces it. CI uses the same name (mission-branch.yml env COVERAGE_MIN).
  COVERAGE_MIN: "80"
  # Shared build directory; comes from the login shell environment (not ~/.cargo/config.toml).
  # Listed here so a runner that scrubs the environment reproduces the same lock behaviour.
  CARGO_TARGET_DIR: /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target
  # Tracing level of the app (see .env.example). Not a secret.
  OBSERVATORY_LOG: info

commands:
  # Nothing is installed per session (mission.md §4): doctor reports tools, hooks sets core.hooksPath.
  install: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory && make doctor && make hooks
  # Per-session preflight (versions, doctor, hooks, branch, worktree symlink, port 3141). Idempotent.
  init: sh /home/user/.factory/missions/e194b9e3-6a67-42b9-bfc9-dd4e1ac23b0c/init.sh
  # The gate: exactly what mission-branch.yml runs (rule 5). A worker hands off only with this green.
  check: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make check
  # No `make typecheck` target exists; cargo check is the fast pass, lint (clippy) is the full one CI runs.
  typecheck: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features
  lint: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make lint
  test: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make test
  fmt: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make fmt
  fmt-check: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make fmt-check
  deny: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make deny
  machete: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo machete
  replay-fixtures: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make replay-fixtures
  # MUST RUN ALONE (no other cargo build, trunk rebuild or tauri dev in flight): load 3.3 -> 14.6 on 10 cores.
  # CI runs the same with --all-features --summary-only (architecture §15). S adds `make coverage` for it.
  coverage: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines ${COVERAGE_MIN:-80}
  # Release build of every crate (cargo build --workspace --release).
  build: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make build
  # Local desktop bundle: `.app` only (bundle.targets ["app"], planning note 3). DMG exists only in CI's bundle job.
  app-build: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make app-build
  # Headless oracle the validators compare the UI against (exit code and the final `unknown events: N` line).
  replay: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay
  inspect: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect
  metrics-csv: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- metrics --csv
  # Fixtures are committed only after this is clean and a reviewer read them (planning notes, off-limits list).
  gitleaks-fixtures: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && gitleaks detect --no-git --no-banner --redact --source fixtures/streams
  # Close every agent-browser daemon at the end of a validation (idle timeout is otherwise 1 h).
  browser-close-all: agent-browser close --all

services:
  trunk-ui:
    # Browser host of the Leptos UI (primary validation surface, SPEC §6). Trunk.toml lives at
    # apps/observatory-app/ui/Trunk.toml (architecture §2, §7) and already says port = 3141, open = false;
    # the flags repeat them so a stale config cannot move the port. Flag spelling: `--open false`, not `--open=false`.
    # Cold start 55.94 s (first dev wasm build), incremental rebuild 1.46-2.08 s. Steady state 35 MB RSS.
    start: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current/apps/observatory-app && trunk serve --config ui/Trunk.toml --port 3141 --open false > /tmp/observatory-trunk-3141.log 2>&1
    stop: lsof -ti :3141 | xargs kill
    healthcheck: curl -sf http://localhost:3141/ > /dev/null
    # Ready when the log shows `INFO success` after `starting build`; the port answers from then on.
    log: /tmp/observatory-trunk-3141.log
    port: 3141
    depends_on: []

  tauri-dev:
    # Native window smoke surface (planning note 4). `make app-dev` = `cargo tauri dev`; tauri-cli finds
    # apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json from the worktree root and runs beforeDevCommand
    # (`trunk serve --config ui/Trunk.toml --port 3141 --open false`) from apps/observatory-app, then
    # `cargo run` for the shell. 37.66 s to the app process with warm wasm (31.18 s native build).
    # Stop trunk-ui first: exactly one trunk may own 3141. The trunk this service starts also serves
    # agent-browser validators on 3141.
    start: cd /home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/observatory-wt/current && make app-dev > /tmp/observatory-tauri.log 2>&1
    # Killing cargo-tauri alone orphans `trunk serve` and the app binary (both reparent to PID 1 and
    # trunk keeps 3141 bound). Kill all three by PID, then free 3141.
    # The debug binary is $CARGO_TARGET_DIR/debug/observatory-app (package name, not productName).
    stop: >-
      pids=$(ps -axo pid=,command= | awk '$2 ~ /(^|\/)cargo-tauri$/ || ($2 ~ /(^|\/)trunk$/ && $3 == "serve") || $2 ~ /\/debug\/observatory-app$/ { print $1 }');
      [ -n "$pids" ] && kill $pids;
      sleep 1;
      lsof -ti :3141 | xargs kill 2>/dev/null;
      true
    # Alive = `Running .../debug/observatory-app` in the log with no panic after it, the app process present,
    # and 3141 answering (the WKWebView fetches the page from it). agent-browser cannot attach (no CDP).
    # cargo colours the log (`\e[1m\e[92m     Running\e[0m`), so strip ANSI codes before grep (user-testing-validator-s).
    healthcheck: >-
      perl -pe 's/\e\[[0-9;]*m//g' /tmp/observatory-tauri.log | grep -q 'Running .*/debug/observatory-app'
      && ps -axo pid=,command= | awk '$2 ~ /\/debug\/observatory-app$/ { found = 1 } END { exit !found }'
      && curl -sf http://localhost:3141/ > /dev/null
    log: /tmp/observatory-tauri.log
    port: 3141
    depends_on: []

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

Rule 19: orchestrator, worker and validator models are declared in the spec and the
mission command; a change is a decision file. The owner set the roles on 2026-10-22.

## Decision

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny and user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Declared in `.factory/settings.json` (`missionOrchestratorModel`,
`missionModelSettings.workerModel`, `missionModelSettings.validationWorkerModel`), the
README mission command, `config/observatory.example.toml` `[mission]`, and the price table
`config/prices/2026-10-22.toml`. Reasoning effort per role is set in `SPEC.md` §2.

**2026-10-22 correction:** Factory's catalog ID is `claude-fable-5.1`; `claude-fable-5-1` was a spelling error that caused fallback to GPT-6 Sol, not a change of intended model.
Source: [Factory model catalog](https://docs.factory.com/models.md).

## Alternatives

Same model for all roles (simpler, loses the cost/quality split the observatory is meant
to measure); cheaper validators (validation is where correctness is bought).

## Consequences

Lane 9 compares roles across these three models from the first mission. Changing any of
them: new decision file, update the four places above.
# D-011: cargo-deny exceptions for the Leptos and Tauri dependency trees

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted (worker decision at the S scaffold; the owner reviews it at the S boundary)

## Context

`deny.toml` was written before any dependency existed. The first `cargo deny check` over
the workspace (Leptos 0.8.22, Tauri 2.12.5, core with all features) failed with:

- licence `BSL-1.0` of `xxhash-rust` 0.8.19, pulled in by Leptos `server_fn`;
- advisory RUSTSEC-2024-0436 (`paste` 1.0.15 unmaintained), a build-time proc-macro used by
  Leptos, with no safe upgrade available;
- advisory RUSTSEC-2024-0370 (`proc-macro-error` 1.0.4 unmaintained), reached only through
  the GTK crates Tauri uses on Linux.

Rule 6 and `deny.toml` make any new licence or ignored advisory a decision file.

## Decision

- Allow `BSL-1.0` (Boost Software Licence, permissive, OSI approved).
- Ignore RUSTSEC-2024-0436 with the reason recorded in `deny.toml`.
- Set `[graph].targets` to `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `x86_64-apple-darwin` and
  `wasm32-unknown-unknown`: the app is bundled for macOS only (`bundle.targets = ["app"]`)
  and the UI compiles to wasm. The Linux GTK tree, the only path to RUSTSEC-2024-0370, is
  not part of anything shipped.

## Alternatives

Ignore RUSTSEC-2024-0370 as well and keep all targets (checks code nobody ships, and the
ignore would hide a real advisory if a shipped crate ever pulled it in); drop Leptos (the
UI choice is D-002); `unmaintained = "workspace"` (silences every transitive unmaintained
advisory, including future ones nobody reviewed).

## Consequences

Any new licence, ignored advisory or target still needs a decision file. Remove the
RUSTSEC-2024-0436 ignore when Leptos drops `paste`. Linux support would need the target
list revisited and RUSTSEC-2024-0370 decided.

Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
from this mission's own files.

**Common to every milestone.**

- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).

  sessions live in `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.children/<session-id>.jsonl` with the
  `.settings.json` beside each. A fixture is committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the

`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,

the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).

### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping

`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
path, byte_offset, byte_len }` (appendix A has `path, byte_offset`; `byte_len` is added so a line
can be read without scanning for the newline) is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line
(PRD §11.2: the lane is a view). `mapping_version: MappingVersion` is a second addition to
appendix A: every `Event` names the mapper that produced it, so the first Droid upgrade shows as a
rising unknown-event count against a known version, never as a silently broken board (owner,
entry 23). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion`
selected from the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the
latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
contract of a version.

latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
contract of a version.

## 6. Tests

Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.

| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |

| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |

**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
a decision file.

## 7. CI

Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).

**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
decision file.

**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.

**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
`main`.

**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).

# Rules

The rules this project inherits, adapted for a build run as a Factory Mission (orchestrator, workers, validators) with the human as owner. Derived from the artstudio set (14-oct-2026); rules that only made sense for a hand-run team are struck, not deleted, so the decision is visible.

1. **Tests before code.** No production code without a failing test that asks for it. Workers write the test first and commit it red; validators check that the red run exists in the log. Tests are the contract between the spec and the build.
2. **A walking skeleton first.** The thinnest end-to-end slice (core crate, canonical event model, `observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is on the mission branch before any milestone deepens its area, so every integration is checked by real acceptance tests.
3. **Versions verified, latest stable.** Every crate, tool and image is pinned to a version checked against the official source on the day it is added; the spec's version table says when.
4. **No secrets, no magic values.** Credentials only from the OS keychain or the environment, never in the repo, the store or the logs; every number (poll interval, stall threshold, price) comes from configuration with a stated default and a reason in the spec.
5. **Everything from a clean clone.** `cargo test`, `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay <fixture>` and the app build work on a machine that has only the Rust toolchain and the Tauri prerequisites; the README's commands are the ones CI runs.
6. **CI is a gate, not infrastructure.** Light checks on the mission branch: `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, the replay fixtures, `cargo deny` (advisories and licences), gitleaks. The full attested run on the one pull request into `main`: everything above plus Semgrep (SAST), Trivy filesystem scan on `Cargo.lock`, Checkov on the workflows themselves, an SBOM (`syft` or `cargo-sbom`), the Tauri bundle built on macOS, build provenance with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, cosign-signed artifacts, with the Trivy results and the SBOM attached to the release. It never deploys.
7. **Counts come off the tool.** Test counts, timings, token usage and scan results are pasted from the run that produced them, never estimated.
8. **The spec is as-built.** When the code and the spec disagree at the end of a milestone, the spec is updated in the same integration, with the reason in `docs/decisions/`.
9. **Deviations are the human's to approve.** The orchestrator proposes, with reason and cost, and waits.
10. **Honest time.** The README states the real time and usage spent per milestone; what was left out is listed, not hidden.
11. **CI under three minutes warm on the mission branch.** Independent jobs in parallel, cargo and tool caches, prebuilt actions; the heavy stage only on the final pull request. Measured per run and reported.
12. **Git forward only, one PR per mission.** Never amend, reset, rebase or stash; a mistake is fixed by a new commit. Milestones live in worktrees and are integrated into `mission/<name>`; nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. A milestone is never shippable; the mission is.
13. **One file per decision, no shared files across worktrees.** `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` (what, why, alternatives, consequences); the index is generated. Two worktrees never edit the same file; the living spec sections are written by the orchestrator on the mission branch at integration time.
14. **Review fixes what blocks.** Blocking and security findings are fixed in the milestone, once; everything else goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`) with its reason. A review never starts a second round for style.
15. **Nothing reaches an agent mid-task.** Decisions are settled before a milestone starts; what comes up later waits for the next milestone or goes to the backlog. The human messages the mission only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up.
16. **Deliverables grow with the work.** README, decisions, backlog, build-log and the session log start with the skeleton and are extended at every integration, never written at the end.
17. **Everything is logged.** Hooks record every tool call to `build-log/`; every session transcript is linked from the session log; usage per model and per milestone is recorded. The build of the observatory is itself a dataset for the observatory.
18. **Unknown is surfaced, never dropped.** An event the mapper does not recognise is counted and shown; a milestone that adds a source ends with zero unknown events on its capture.
19. **Models per role are declared.** Orchestrator, worker and validator models are named in the spec and in the mission command; a change of model is a decision file.

Struck from the artstudio set: *tester, coder and reviewer as separate agents per team* (the Mission's workers and validators take those roles; if the validators prove weaker, custom sub-droids bring the split back, as a decision); *the 90-minute box* (replaced by usage budgets per milestone).
=====
# Backlog

Deferred items with their reasons (ai/RULES.md rule 14). Reference as `B-NNN` from code
(`TODO(B-NNN)`) and decisions. Scheduled items move to the spec; dropped items stay here with
the reason struck through, not deleted.

| Id | Item | Reason deferred | Earliest |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-001 | Devcontainer for Linux CI parity | Tauri on macOS is the target; a container cannot run the window. Useful for core-only work. `.devcontainer/` provisions `make check` tools and the Linux Tauri libraries. | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-002 | CI telemetry to Grafana (workflow durations, test timings) via OTLP | Owner: document only for now. Secret `GRAFANA_OTLP_HEADERS`, variable `GRAFANA_OTLP_ENDPOINT` reserved. | after M5 |
| B-003 | Dedicated error tracking (Sentry or Grafana Faro) | D-004 uses span events first; add a tracker only if they prove insufficient. | after M2 |
| B-004 | Release notes automation (git-cliff from conventional-ish subjects) | ~~No releases until the mission PR; one PR means one changelog entry.~~ Done differently: GitHub-generated notes by label plus `release.yml` on tags (D-009). | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-005 | Coverage thresholds (`cargo-llvm-cov`, fail under a stated %) | Settled: 80 % lines on observatory-core, enforced from M0 (SPEC §6). | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-006 | Log scrubbing utility for raw JSONL rendering | PRD renders raw lines read-only; a redaction pass before display is the next step. | M1 |
| B-007 | Demo branch pair in this repo (`demo/base`, `demo/*`, `demo-gate.yml`, label `demo:red`) for M4 | Set up by the mission before M4 (SPEC §3 M4). | before M4 |
| B-008 | Human-computed reference spreadsheet from the M0 capture for M5, at `reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv` | Mission input; cannot be produced by validators (SPEC §3 M5). | before M5 |
| B-009 | Optional manual ~20-minute mission capture before the mission starts | ~~Insurance for M0 planning, not structural.~~ Not needed: the capture is this mission's own sessions (SPEC §3). | dropped 2026-10-22 |
| B-010 | Settle walking-skeleton vs M0 boundary in SPEC.md | Settled: skeleton S before M0; capture = this mission's sessions (SPEC §3). | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-011 | Fill `config/prices/2026-10-22.toml` from the vendor price page, set `verified = true` | Prices must be read on the day, not recalled. | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-012 | Runbook: stalled mission, red gate, fix cycle, hooks disabled | `docs/runbooks/` written with CLI steps; app steps marked with the milestone that delivers them. Revise at M3. | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-013 | GitHub code scanning default setup (CodeQL) | Default setup enabled (languages detected: actions; Rust joins when code exists). Semgrep and Trivy SARIF uploaded from the gate. | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-014 | Dead code and unused dependency checks (`cargo-udeps`, `cargo-machete`) in the mission-branch CI | Settled: cargo-machete on the mission branch, no udeps (SPEC §7). | done 2026-10-22 |
| B-015 | Readiness report re-run at every milestone integration, stored in `reports/readiness/` | Baseline exists; cadence belongs to the spec. | each milestone |
| B-016 | `release.yml` checks that the `Cargo.toml` workspace version equals the tag | Needs `Cargo.toml` (D-009). | with skeleton |
| B-017 | Spec states the exported metric set, histogram buckets and the computed active-series count, under 200 (D-010) | Settled: 182 series worst case, 124 expected, buckets in SPEC §5.7. | done 2026-10-22 |

# droid-observatory

A Rust desktop app that watches a Factory Mission build a business feature: which agent is on
what, whether each milestone is validated, where time and tokens go, and the one gate that
ships it. Lanes are the mission's orchestrated states; cards are milestones; the last lane is
the pull request into `main`.

**Status:** pre-mission. The repository holds the PRD, the rules, the CI gate and the
configuration contract. No application code yet: the walking skeleton is the mission's first
integration (ai/RULES.md rule 2). Rust targets in the `Makefile` activate the moment a
`Cargo.toml` lands.

## What it will show

| Lane | Holds |
|---|---|
| 1 Intent | prompt, spec, acceptance criteria, re-prompts |
| 2 Orchestrator | plan, milestones, task assignment, replans |
| 3 Workers | one sub-lane per worker: files, tests, commits |
| 4 Validators, scrutiny | findings, blocking vs non-blocking, rework |
| 5 Validators, user testing | QA scenarios against the built thing |
| 6 Integration | worktree landings on `mission/<name>`, fast checks |
| 7 Human | approvals, answers, the review, the merge |
| 8 Outside | the PR, CI, attestations, deploys |
| 9 Time, waste, cost, models | tokens per role, waste by cause, budget |

Full definition: [ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md](ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md).
Spec: [SPEC.md](SPEC.md) (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

## From a clean clone

Requirements: the Rust toolchain via [rustup](https://rustup.rs) (version pinned in
`rust-toolchain.toml`), and the tools `make doctor` lists.

```sh
git clone user@example.invalid:dctellya/droid-observatory.git
cd droid-observatory
make doctor      # which tools are missing and how to install them
make hooks       # enable the git hooks (once)
make check       # every light check the mission-branch CI runs
```

`make help` lists all targets. The same targets run in CI, so a documented command is a
command the gate runs.

## Commands

| Target | What it does | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `make check` | all light checks below | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-docs` | markdownlint on every `.md` | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-links` | lychee link check | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-workflows` | actionlint | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-file-size` | tracked files under 200 KB (fixtures exempt) | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-todos` | debt markers must cite `#issue` or `B-nnn` | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-decisions-index` | `docs/decisions/README.md` is generated and current | mission branch, gate |
| `make check-secrets` | gitleaks over the repository | mission branch, gate |
| `make fmt-check` / `make lint` / `make test` / `make deny` | rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, cargo-deny | once `Cargo.toml` exists |
| `make replay-fixtures` | every `fixtures/streams/*.jsonl` through `observatory-cli replay` | once fixtures exist |
| `make app-dev` / `make app-build` | Tauri dev window / macOS bundle | once the app exists |

## Configuration

- `config/observatory.example.toml`: every runtime key with its default and reason. Copy to
  `~/.droid-observatory/config.toml`.
- `config/prices/<date>.toml`: the dated price table that turns tokens into money. Each cost on
  the board names the table it used.
- `.env.example`: environment variables, including the Grafana Cloud OTLP contract. Secrets go
  in the OS keychain on the desktop; the environment is the fallback and what CI uses.

## Running it as a mission

Models per role (ai/RULES.md rule 19, `.factory/settings.json`, D-006):
orchestrator `claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`.

```sh
droid exec --mission --auto high \
  --model claude-fable-5.1          --reasoning-effort high \
  --worker-model claude-sonnet-5-5  --worker-reasoning-effort high \
  --validator-model claude-opus-5-5 --validator-reasoning-effort high \
  --output-format text \
  -f SPEC.md
```

Reasoning effort per role is `high` for all three (SPEC §2). The mission works on
`mission/<name>`, one worktree per milestone, and ends in one pull request into `main`.

## The gate

Two workflows, one required check:

- `mission-branch.yml` on `mission/**`: docs, links, workflows, secrets, and (once code
  exists) fmt, clippy, tests, replay fixtures, cargo-deny. Aggregate job `mission-checks`.
  Budget: three minutes warm.
- `gate.yml` on pull requests to `main`: everything above plus Semgrep, Trivy, Checkov on the
  workflows, an SBOM, the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`) with build provenance and cosign
  signatures. Semgrep and Trivy findings are uploaded to GitHub code scanning, which is also
  enabled in default setup. Aggregate job `gate`, the only check the `main` ruleset
  requires. It never deploys.
- `release.yml` on tags `v*` pushed by the human to a commit on `main`: builds the same
  bundle and creates the GitHub release with notes generated from PR labels
  (`.github/release.yml`, D-009). Runbook: `docs/runbooks/release.md`.

Branch rules on `main`: pull request required, `gate` required, no force pushes, no admin
bypass, zero required approvals (the human in lane 7 merges by hand, the gate is the review).

## Observability

Grafana Cloud over OTLP is the telemetry backend (D-004): the app's own traces and metrics,
and the lane-9 mission series (`observatory.*`). Off by default; the app works fully offline.
Endpoint and credentials come from `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` or the keychain, never from the
repository.

## Repository layout

```text
ai/            PRD, rules, spec template, session logs (the human-agent record)
.factory/      mission model settings, hooks: git guard and tool-call logger
.github/       workflows (mission-branch, gate, bundle, release), CODEOWNERS, templates
.githooks/     pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push (enable with `make hooks`)
.devcontainer/ Linux container with every `make check` tool (core work; the window needs macOS)
config/        example config and dated price tables
docs/decisions/ one file per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks/  red gate, fix cycle, stalled mission, hooks disabled, release
build-log/     one JSON line per agent tool call, by day and session
reports/       readiness reports, usage and waste per milestone (pasted from the tool)
scripts/       the checks the Makefile calls
BACKLOG.md     deferred items with their reasons
```

## Honest time

Rule 10: real time and usage per milestone, stated here as the work lands.

| Phase | Wall time | Sessions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ideation → PRD v0.2 | ~1 h 40 m | 1 Droid session | two review rounds; log in `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` |
| Repo readiness | ~2 h | same session | readiness Level 1 (5/65) → Level 3 (31/65); see `reports/readiness/` |

Token usage for these sessions is recorded by Factory, not by this repository yet; the
observatory's first job is to make that number visible.

## Licence

Apache-2.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

#!/bin/sh
# Factory PostToolUse hook: append one compact JSON line per tool call to build-log/
# (ai/RULES.md rule 17). Records what was called, never the tool response, so the
# log stays small and cannot leak tool output.
set -u
input=$(cat)
root=${FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR:-$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.cwd')}
day=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)
dir="$root/build-log/$day"
mkdir -p "$dir"
session=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.session_id // "unknown"')
printf '%s' "$input" | jq -c --arg ts "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" '{
  ts: $ts,
  session_id: .session_id,
  event: .hook_event_name,
  tool: .tool_name,
  command: (.tool_input.command // null),
  file: (.tool_input.file_path // null),
  summary: (.tool_input.summary // null),
  exit_code: (.tool_response.exitCode // null)
}' >> "$dir/$session.jsonl"
exit 0
{
  "PreToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "Execute",
      "commandRegex": "git ",
      "hooks": [
        { "type": "command", "command": "\"$FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR\"/.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh", "timeout": 10 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "PostToolUse": [
    {
      "matcher": "*",
      "hooks": [
        { "type": "command", "command": "\"$FACTORY_PROJECT_DIR\"/.factory/hooks/log-tool-call.sh", "timeout": 10 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

**What belongs here:** everything known about the files Droid 0.247.0 writes under `~/.factory/sessions/`,
which `mapping::v1` reads (planning note 1, dependency readiness report, architecture §4-§5), plus the
fixture layout and header. Facts are from the readiness report or from a keys-only inspection of this
mission's own session directory at drafting time (2026-10-22, 24 `.jsonl`); values were not read except
tag names, model ids, tool names and `subagent_type`. Items marked "M0 to confirm" are frozen by the M0
mapping worker in the decision file.

**What does not belong here:** the mapping table itself (architecture §5 and `mapping/v1/kinds.rs`), Rust
conventions, environment facts other than the directory path.

## Directory and file set

- Directory: `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/` where the slug is the working directory with `/` replaced by
  `-`: `~/.factory/sessions/-home-user-code-EllyaOrg-projects-dalimaray-droid-observatory/`.
- Flat: no subdirectories. Child sessions are sibling files.
- Per session `<session-id>` (UUID): `<id>.jsonl` (the transcript), `<id>.settings.json` (the sidecar),
  `<id>.settings.json.bak`. Counts at drafting: 72 entries = 24 of each. The readiness report saw 12, then
  14 `.jsonl`.
- There is no Droid version anywhere in these files. The mapping version is selected from `droid_version` in
  the fixture header (`0.247.*` maps to `V1`; anything else gives `LATEST` with
  `Warning::UnknownDroidVersion`); a live attach records `droid --version` into the `captures` row.
- The directory is read-only for the mission. Fixtures are byte-identical copies.

## JSONL line types

`type` values and counts over the 24 files at drafting:

```text
3890 message
  54 agent_turn_outcome
  37 todo_state
  24 session_start
   5 compaction_state
```

### `session_start` (first line of each file)

Keys observed (two shapes):

```text
["callingSessionId","callingToolUseId","cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","title","type","version"]   child
["cwd","hostId","id","isSessionTitleManuallySet","organizationId","owner","sessionTitleAutoStage","title","type","version"]                root
```

- `version` is the numeric schema version: `2` on all 24 files. It is not the Droid version.
- `callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId` are the parent linkage: a file whose `callingSessionId` equals a
  known session id is a child; the root has none. At drafting: 2 roots, 22 children. The root `id` is the
  mission id used by the mapper (`mission_id` = root session id).
- `callingToolUseId` matches the `id` of a `tool_use` part (tool `Task`) in the parent's transcript; the two id
  styles seen are `toolu_bdrk_...` and `call_...`.

### `message`

Top-level keys: `id, message, parentId, seq, timestamp, type` (3601 lines); 265 lines add
`compactionSummaryId`; the 24 first messages have no `parentId`. `timestamp` is RFC 3339.

`message` object keys:

- user: `content, role, visibility` and often `userMessageSource`.
- assistant: `apiProvider, content, modelId, reasoningEffort, role` (211 lines carry these three model keys).
  `modelId` values at drafting: `claude-fable-5.1` (369), `gpt-6.1-sol` (23), `gpt-6-sol` (15).
  A change of `modelId` between consecutive assistant messages of one session is `ModelChanged`.

`content[]` part `type` counts: `tool_use` 1661, `tool_result` 1659, `text` 410, `thinking` 263.
`tool_use` parts: `{id, name, input}`; `tool_result`: `{tool_use_id, content, is_error?}`.
Tool names seen (architecture §5): `Task`, `Execute`, `Script`, `Read`, `Edit`, `Create`, `Grep`, `Glob`,
`LS`, `TodoWrite`, `AskUser`, `ProposeMission`, `Skill`, `FetchUrl`, `WaitForScript`, `ApplyPatch`.

`Task` input keys observed: `await, complexity, description, prompt, subagent_type` (16), without
`complexity` (4), without `await` (2). `subagent_type` values: `worker` (20), `explorer` (2). No validator
spawn exists yet in this directory; the exact `subagent_type` strings for the scrutiny and user-testing
validators are **M0 to confirm** from the S capture.

Keys `reason, resultKind, turnId, type`. `resultKind` values: `text` (42), `null` (12). In a child session it
maps to `TaskDone`, then `SubagentFinished` at EOF.

### `todo_state`

Keys `id, messageIndex, timestamp, todos, type`. Maps to `PlanRevised` when the todos changed.

### `compaction_state`

Keys `anchorMessage, id, loadedDeferredToolNames, removedCount, retainedImages, retainedSkills, summaryKind,

# D-012: Droid session schema and the input of the mapping

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-22, entry 26; recorded at the S integration)

## Context

PRD §11.1 left open where Droid records its version, tags, child sessions and usage. The
dependency readiness report (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`) and the S
fixture (`fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.*`, Droid 0.247.0) settled it by
inspection of the session directory:

- No session file carries the Droid version. `session_start.version` is the numeric schema
  version (`2`), not the Droid release.
- Usage is not in the JSONL. There are no `usage.reported` lines; token counts live in the
  sibling `<session-id>.settings.json`.
- `tags` in the sidecar is an array of objects `{ "name": <string>, "metadata": <object|null> }`,
  not strings. Seen: `mission-session` with `metadata.role`, `subagent` with
  `metadata.callingSessionId` and `callingToolUseId`, `mission-worker`, `exec`, `read-only`.
- Child sessions are sibling files. A child's `session_start.callingSessionId` names its parent;
  `callingToolUseId` is null for workers the mission runner starts.

SPEC §3 M0 and §5.2 said the mapping version was selected from "the Droid version in the session
`.settings.json"`. That cannot work, because the file has no such field (rule 8).

## Decision

- The mapping version is selected from `droid_version` in the fixture header
  `<capture>.capture.json` (written at capture time from `droid --version`; a live attach records
  `droid --version` into the `captures` row). `0.247.x` selects `mapping::v1`. An unknown Droid
  version uses the latest mapping and raises a one-line warning.
- Usage, model, reasoning effort, tags and child links come from the sibling `.settings.json`
  (`tokenUsage`, `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`, `lastCallTokenUsage`,
  `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`, `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`).
  The mapper emits `UsageReported` from the sidecar, once at the end of the stream or when it changes.
- Roles come from `tags[].metadata.role` (orchestrator, worker) and from the `Task` input
  `subagent_type` for sessions a `Task` call started. Parent linkage comes from
  `session_start.callingSessionId`.
- SPEC §3 M0 and §5.2 are amended as-built in the same integration.

## Alternatives

Read a version from the JSONL (there is none); guess the version from line shapes (a silent
mis-selection is exactly what the versioned mapper exists to prevent, F-007); require users to
pass the version on the command line (a captured file would stop replaying by itself).

## Consequences

Every fixture needs a `.capture.json` with `droid_version` and a sidecar per session, and a
fixture is never replayed without its header. A Droid release that changes either file shape
shows up as a rising unknown-event count against a known version. M0 confirms the remaining open
items of PRD §11.1 (exact validator `subagent_type` strings, feature and milestone ids) in
`docs/decisions/D-0NN-mapping-v1.md`.

# D-013: keyring variant B, `keyring-core` with `apple-native-keyring-store`

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-22, entry 26; recorded at the S integration)

## Context

The app reads the GitHub token and the OTLP headers from the OS keychain (rule 4). `keyring`
4.2.0 with default features fails `cargo deny`: RUSTSEC-2026-0370, RUSTSEC-2026-0371 and
RUSTSEC-2026-0372 (zbus and zvariant unmaintained), reached on the Linux path through
`zbus-secret-service-keyring-store` (`reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).
The app ships for macOS only. Both items exist in the keychain as generic passwords with service
`droid-observatory/<name>` and account `dct`.

## Decision

Use variant B: `keyring-core` 1.0.1 and `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 with feature
`keychain`, selected with `set_default_store`, behind `observatory_core::secrets` (feature
`secrets`). Never `keyring` 4.x. Both crates are declared in the workspace `Cargo.toml` and
listed in `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored` until the secrets module uses them.

## Alternatives

`keyring` 4.2.0 with default features (fails `cargo deny`); `keyring` 4.2.0 with the Linux
backends off (still a larger tree than the store needs); calling the macOS `security` CLI
(a process per read, and the value would pass through a pipe).

## Consequences

Linux has no secret store; there the environment variable is the only source (what CI uses).
The `security find-generic-password` lookups in tests use the full service string
`droid-observatory/<name>` and never `-w`. When the secrets module lands the machete ignore
entries are removed.

# D-014: Read-only fine-grained PAT, check results from Actions runs and commit statuses

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-22, entry 26; recorded at the S integration)

## Context

The gate lane needs the state of CI for a branch and a pull request. The token in the keychain
(`droid-observatory/github-token`) is a fine-grained personal access token for owner `dctellya`,
repositories `droid-observatory` and `artstudio`, read-only on Contents, Issues, Pull requests,
Actions, Commit statuses and Metadata. Fine-grained tokens have no Checks permission, so
`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/check-runs` is not available (entry 26).

## Decision

- Read check results from Actions runs (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>`) and
  commit statuses (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`). Never call the Checks API.
- The token stays read-only. The one outward write, merge, is not attempted by default: the app
  shows the Merge button when policy allows, surfaces the `403` cleanly (message naming the PR,
  the target and the missing permission, no crash, no retry storm), and the owner merges in the
  GitHub UI or API; the badge updates from the poll (owner decision 2026-10-22, planning note 7).
- Whether to give the app a write-capable token is asked at the M3 to M4 boundary.

## Alternatives

A classic token with `repo` scope (broad, can write everywhere); a GitHub App (setup cost for a
single-user desktop tool); the `gh` CLI as the transport (an external process in the hot path, and
the token would live in the CLI's store, not the keychain item the PRD names).

## Consequences

Required-check names come from the ruleset and workflow job names, not from check runs. A check
that reports only through the Checks API and not as an Actions run or a status is invisible to the
app. SPEC §3 M4 acceptance is amended as-built in the same integration.

# D-015: The backlog is BACKLOG.md only; the hybrid backlog is withdrawn

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner comment on the mission proposal, 2026-10-22, entry 27)

## Context

SPEC §8 planned a hybrid backlog: GitHub issues labelled `backlog` created at S integration, with
`scripts/gen-backlog.sh` regenerating `BACKLOG.md` from them. That reopened the Issues question
the owner had closed the day before: deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md`, not to GitHub issues
(AGENTS.md, rule 14 as the owner reads it). The owner asked to pick `BACKLOG.md` only, "unless you
want Issues back on purpose" (entry 27, comment 4).

## Decision

`BACKLOG.md` is the only backlog. No issue is created, no `backlog` label exists, and
`scripts/gen-backlog.sh` is not written. Deferred items are `B-NNN` rows with a reason and an
"earliest" column; settled rows are marked done with the date, dropped rows are struck through.
The integration feature writes new rows from the workers' handoffs. SPEC §8 is amended as-built.

## Alternatives

Hybrid backlog (two sources of truth and an issue-creating mission the owner did not ask for);
issues only (loses the offline, reviewable-in-PR history that `BACKLOG.md` gives).

## Consequences

`ai/RULES.md` rule 14 still reads "GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`".
The file is the owner's; the proposed wording is "everything else goes to `BACKLOG.md` with its
reason", and its change is on the S to M0 boundary list.

# D-016: Line coverage of observatory-core, 80 % from M0, cargo-llvm-cov

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (SPEC §6 as settled in B-005; wired in S, enforced from the M0 integration)

## Context

B-005 asked for a coverage threshold. `observatory-core` holds every piece of logic that can be
wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost). The CLI is thin and has its own tests, and the UI
crate compiles to wasm and holds no logic. At S the core is small: the scaffold reported
95.92 % lines (`make coverage`), but a percentage over so little code means little.

## Decision

- Component: `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.9.1, `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --all-features
  --fail-under-lines <COVERAGE_MIN> --summary-only`, in its own `coverage` job in
  `mission-branch.yml` and as `make coverage`. The job installs `llvm-tools-preview` on the
  toolchain pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- Threshold: 80 % lines on `observatory-core` only. S reports it with `COVERAGE_MIN` at `"0"`;
  the M0 integration sets it to `"80"`. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason; lowering it is
  a decision file.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone on the machine (load 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores in the readiness run).
- If the warm `mission-checks` time exceeds 3 minutes once coverage joins, coverage moves to the
  final pull request only, by decision file (SPEC §7).

## Alternatives

`tarpaulin` (ptrace on Linux only, not the macOS developer machine); a threshold on the whole
workspace (the UI crate drags it down for no information); branch coverage (nightly only).

## Consequences

The coverage job hard-codes the toolchain version for `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, so it must change
together with `rust-toolchain.toml` (BACKLOG B-018). IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub
cannot all run in CI; that is the 20 % of room.

# D-017: cargo-machete for unused dependencies, not cargo-udeps

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (SPEC §7 as settled in B-014; wired in S)

## Context

B-014 asked for a dead-dependency check in the mission-branch CI. `cargo-udeps` needs a nightly
toolchain, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache. `cargo-machete` 0.9.2 runs on stable in
seconds.

## Decision

`cargo machete` is part of `make check` and a `machete` job of `mission-checks`
(`taiki-e/install-action`, `cargo-machete@0.9.2`). A dependency declared ahead of use sits in that
package's `[package.metadata.cargo-machete] ignored` list; the first module that uses it removes the
entry. No dependency is added to the list to silence a crate nobody plans to use. At the S
integration the lists hold `rusqlite`, `keyring-core` and `apple-native-keyring-store` (core) and
`tokio` and `observatory-core` (src-tauri).

## Alternatives

`cargo-udeps` (nightly; finds a strict superset only in edge cases); no check (declared-ahead
dependencies would rot unnoticed).

## Consequences

Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency. A feature that starts using an ignored crate
must delete its entry in the same commit, or the ignore hides a later removal.

# D-018: The models and reasoning efforts of a mission are invariant

**Date:** 2026-10-23
**Status:** accepted (owner decision 2026-10-23 at the S to M0 boundary)

## Context

Rule 19 says models per role are declared and a change is a decision file. D-006 declared them for
this mission. Facts from the S to M0 boundary:

- On 2026-10-22 at 19:55 local time the Factory usage overage switched the mission's
  `model-settings.json` to `kimi-k3` for workers and validators (`workerModel` and
  `validationWorkerModel`), without anyone asking for it.
- Worker session `82a61cf6` for `m0-integrate-s` started on `kimi-k3` at 2026-10-23T06:40:42Z and
  ended with an error at 07:13:30Z, with zero commits.
- The model of the resumed user-testing-validator-s session (`d0304e2e`, resumed at 06:40Z) is not
  recorded.
- After the owner restored the settings, the orchestrator restarted this feature on the approved
  models. This session is the second start of `m0-integrate-s`.

## Decision

INVARIANT: the models and reasoning efforts defined at mission approval (orchestrator
`claude-fable-5.1`, workers `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`, all `high`; D-006)
never change for the lifetime of the mission.

- When a Factory usage limit (5-hour, 7-day or monthly) is reached, the mission stops and waits for
  the owner. It never continues on a fallback or core model.
- The overage preference is "stop", never "switch".
- Before a resume the owner restores the mission model settings (`model-settings.json`: workers
  `claude-sonnet-5-5`, validators `claude-opus-5-5`, both `high`) and the orchestrator verifies them.
- A worker that started on another model is restarted from scratch, never resumed.
- Every such episode is recorded in the session log.

## Alternatives

Continue on the fallback model (rejected: it breaks rule 19 and makes usage and cost attribution
per model meaningless); continue on the fallback and note it in the report (the reports would
then mix models under a role, and a validator weaker than the approved one would pass work the
approved one might fail).

## Consequences

A usage limit costs wall time, not quality or attribution. `ai/RULES.md` rule 20 states the same
invariant for any mission. Each integration checks `.factory/settings.json` and the model ids in
`reports/usage/<m>.md` (VAL-PROC-027).
